turn_text: I would tell you that Ohio's 16th District is very lucky to have you because you are really doing a good job. So that leads me to your bill, the Jobs Act, that expands access to trade in career college education. Tell us a little bit more about that legislation and why it's so important.

So the biggest challenge that I hear from employers in my district today is workforce. Folks either can't find people with the right skills or they can't get people through a drug test or there aren't folks coming off the sideline, whatever it is, everybody is dealing with a different workforce challenge and that's across every industry. And so, you know, my thought there was, okay, you know, what do you do about that? Do you create another federal program? I'm not super excited about, you know, one more federal program. Or do you look at what's there and try to find a way to get more flexibility? And so that's where the Jobs Act kind of logic comes from from my standpoint. Senator Portman introduced it on the Senate side. and I read through and so this is exactly what I'm looking for and what it would do is it would allow Pell grants to be used for some of these short-term training programs, certificate programs that are managed at the state level. So I think that's fantastic. It gives flexibility to states to say here's the jobs that we need and here are the programs that apply and then it empowers the individual to go directly to the programs that are best for them.
